themes.beneath: In proportion, for the desk's size calls, judged at Friday's close against Nov 13's: Nvidia at $145.98 is 10.38% below $162.89, past its 7.5% line; AMD at $489.19 is 8.19% below $532.84, 0.81 points short of its 9% line ($484.88); Dell at $312.54 (Yahoo's last price; its daily bar is empty) is 8.88% below $342.98, 0.62 points short of its 9.5% line ($310.40). After hours Nvidia is -0.9% and AMD -3.4%. The calls are sizes either way; Friday's close decides them.
themes.cause: From +1.3% before the open to -2.0% at the close for the S&P 500 fund: a swing of over 3 points on the day of the largest listing on record. The AI group closed at its lows: Nvidia -3.3% to $145.98, Marvell -4.9%, Amazon -3.9%, Alphabet -3.5%, Oracle -2.9%, Broadcom -2.1%; AMD -7.7% on a Hunterbrook report alleging ties to a blacklisted Chinese server maker (Motley Fool). All 11 sectors fell (Motley Fool).
themes.mechanism: Anthropic sold about $81 billion of new stock in the offering plus a $26 billion private placement (Fox Business, last note): over $100 billion of new AI shares for investors to buy in one day. My inference is that much of it was paid for by selling other AI holdings, and that once the event the market had bought for had passed, the rest of the market sold with it. Motley Fool raises the same question about how much capital is left for other AI investments (an opinion).
themes.name: The market sold the Anthropic news, and the selling reached every sector
themes.watch: Friday's close against the three call lines; whether Anthropic holds above $83; a seventh down day for the S&P 500 would match the longest run in over two years.

themes.beneath: In proportion: Intuit was worth $83.1 billion; -9.8% is about $8 billion. The Mailchimp loss, about $8.3 billion against its purchase price, is roughly the same size, though it was written down over years; my reading is that the market is pricing the lowered outlook, not the sale.
themes.cause: Intuit fell 9.8% after hours: first-quarter revenue grew 12% and beat its guidance, but it lowered its full-year revenue outlook (MarketBeat on its call) and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion, against the $12 billion it paid in 2021 (Simply Wall St on Yahoo; its 8-K).
themes.mechanism: Application software has fallen through the week as investors weigh what AI models replace (Salesforce -3.7% Thursday, after -2.1% Wednesday). Intuit's cut outlook gives that worry a number; selling a 2021 purchase for about 30 cents on the dollar marks down what such businesses are worth. Stocktwits reads it as fear of AI disruption in software-as-a-service (an opinion).
themes.name: Intuit fell after hours on a lower outlook and Mailchimp's sale at a third of its price
themes.watch: Whether application software follows Intuit lower on Friday.

themes.beneath: Gap rose on a cut outlook, which says its price had already assumed worse; Ross fell on a raised one, which says its price had assumed more. Neither move is about the shopper alone; each is about what the price had assumed.
themes.cause: Consumer discretionary was the worst sector (-2.79%, Motley Fool); Williams-Sonoma closed -15.2% (after reiterating, not raising, its guidance). After hours: Ross -5.2% even after raising its EPS outlook; Gap +3.6% after flat comparable sales, a full-year sales outlook cut to roughly flat from +1-1.5%, and a slower start to the fourth quarter (StockTitan).
themes.mechanism: Wednesday's rally priced relief that holiday shoppers were holding up (TJX, Target). Thursday's reports were weaker at the margin: Gap says the fourth quarter started slowly, Walmart's same-store sales slowed to 2.9%. That the holiday-relief trade is reversing is my inference.
themes.name: Consumer stocks led the fall, and the evening's retail reports cut outlooks
themes.watch: Ross and Gap at Friday's open; whether the off-price names give back Wednesday's gains.

themes.beneath: In proportion: UnitedHealth closed at $412.02 on Monday (TradingKey, earlier note), so $330.48 is a 19.8% fall in three sessions, about $74 billion of value. The proposal's own estimate is about $9 billion a year across the industry.
themes.cause: UnitedHealth closed -5.6% at $330.48 and Cigna -4.3%; Elevance -2.7%, Centene -2.8%, Humana -1.5% (the bank's daily bars). After hours they are flat.
themes.mechanism: No new report; the Medicare Advantage audit proposal of Nov 16 is still the only stated cause, and Thursday's fall came with the whole market's. A correction: the group rose on Monday Nov 16 and fell on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, three sessions. Wednesday night's note called Wednesday the third day and Thursday's midday note called Thursday the fourth; both miscounted (Yahoo's '18% over five days' counts calendar sessions, not down days).
